title: Bi 2 S 3  nanostructures for low temperature NO 2  sensors: insights into work function tuning and band bending effect
content: The rapid increase in environmental pollution from industries and vehicle emissions has led to elevated concentrations of toxic gases, which directly affect the air quality index (AQI). Particularly, nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a harmful pollutant associated with serious respiratory ailments and environmental impacts. Hence, here we investigated the gas sensing performance of Bi2S3 and reported its sensing characteristics towards NO2. The orthorhombic phase and its Raman vibrational modes were confirmed using an X-ray diffraction pattern and Raman spectra. The deformation and associated lattice strain were observed upon La incorporation, and these favours the surface-active sites or NO2 adsorption. The work function (Φ) of 5.255 eV for BLa-3 (3% La-incorporated Bi2S3) and higher surface band bending (ΔqV) synergistically favour the maximum NO2 response of 2684% and good selectivity over other interacting gases.
